author: human
request:
Feature request: the vet list answers "which specialties does this vet hold",
but staff also ask the inverse — "which vets hold this specialty". Two
product decisions come with it, made here as the product owner:

- A read-only specialty view of the existing directory is in scope; managing
  veterinarians or specialties stays out of scope as before (non-goal NG-2
  is unchanged).
- The page is reachable by its URL alone: no navigation entry and no link
  from another page is part of this request. A visible entry point may come
  as a follow-up request.

Add a specialty directory page:

- GET /specialties.html lists every specialty the clinic knows by its stored
  name, each with the veterinarians holding it.
- Each veterinarian is shown by full name: first name, then last name (for
  example "Helen Leary").
- A veterinarian holding no specialty appears under no specialty; the page
  lists specialties, not the full vet roster.
- All specialties render on one page — no pagination.

Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Specialty directory lists every specialty with the veterinarians holding it
summary: A read-only page lists every specialty the clinic knows, each under its stored name, with the veterinarians holding it named in full. One page, no paging, reachable by its address alone.
acceptance_criteria: A request for GET /specialties.html renders a page listing every specialty the clinic knows, each under its stored name.
Each specialty is shown with the veterinarians holding it, each named first name then last name (for example "Helen Leary").
A veterinarian holding no specialty is named nowhere on the page.
A specialty that no veterinarian holds is still listed, with no veterinarian named under it.
When the clinic knows no specialty at all, the page renders with no specialties rather than failing.
Every specialty renders on one page: no paging control, no second page.
Specialties, and the veterinarians within each specialty, render in a stable order across repeated requests.
No navigation entry names the specialty directory, and no other page links to it.
The page's user-facing wording is not hard-coded into the page and is present in every supported language, per REQ-LANG-002.
non_goals: Managing veterinarians or specialties through the application; NG-2 is unchanged and the page is read-only.
Any search or filter input on the page; NG-9 is unchanged.
A navigation entry or a link from another page. The owner deferred a visible entry point to a possible follow-up request.
Changing the existing veterinarian directory or its paging.
notes: Address quoted from the owner (intake line 1): "GET /specialties.html lists every specialty the clinic knows by its stored name, each with the veterinarians holding it." No Non-Goals row changes, so no scope_overrides. Two open questions recorded in docs/prd.md rather than blocked on, per the intake's standing instruction: whether the page should later gain a visible entry point, and whether the listing order should be alphabetical. The narrowest reading was taken for both: no entry point now, and a stable order without a stated sort key. REQ-SYS-001 still binds the new page, so it carries the site navigation to the owner and veterinarian areas like every other page.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The slice lives entirely in the vet feature package and adds a second read surface beside the veterinarian directory. Three things make it new ground rather than a repeat of an existing pattern: Specialty has no repository, the @ManyToMany runs one way from Vet to Specialty so a specialty cannot reach its holders, and the codebase has no read model composing two reads. ADR 2026-08-16 records the choice of in-memory composition over an inverse mapping or a projection query; docs/system-design.md gains four Contracts rows and the package-structure line for vet/. Shape: SpecialtyRepository returns every specialty in name order (PetTypeRepository is the precedent); SpecialtyDirectory is an immutable value object built by a pure static factory from all specialties plus VetRepository.findAll(); SpecialtyController is a package-private @Controller serving GET /specialties.html with no request parameter and one model attribute. Both edge cases fall out of the structure rather than a branch: iterating specialties lists one nobody holds, and grouping by specialty names no veterinarian who holds none.
integration_points: SpecialtyController depends on SpecialtyRepository and the existing VetRepository, both by constructor injection; no existing type is modified.
SpecialtyDirectory.of(specialties, veterinarians) is the single composition point; the controller passes the two reads and adds the result to the model.
The template reuses fragments/layout.html, so REQ-SYS-001 site navigation is present. Pass an active-menu value that matches no menuItem so nothing is highlighted and no nav entry is added.
New message keys go into messages.properties and every non-English locale bundle; messages_en.properties stays empty by the existing fallback convention (I18nPropertiesSyncTest skips it).

patterns.description: Spring Data repository over a lookup entity returning every row in name order — the shape SpecialtyRepository copies. Confirmed by reading the file; no IDE oracle connected, so this is the weaker grep-class basis.
Package-private @Controller, constructor-injected repository, model attributes then a view name — the shape SpecialtyController copies, minus the pagination helper.
Layout fragment invocation and th:each table rendering; the new template follows it without the paging block.

@WebMvcTest slice with @DisabledInNativeImage and @DisabledInAotMode; the controller test follows it. SpecialtyDirectory itself needs no Spring context — test it with real Vet and Specialty objects, no mocks.
getSpecialties() already sorts by name; reuse it rather than re-sorting inside the directory.

risks.risk: Grouping logic drifting into SpecialtyController would be a fresh violation of the Web controller row of the pattern catalog, which the recorded controller-rule deviation does not extend to.
risks.mitigation: All grouping and full-name formatting live in SpecialtyDirectory's static factory; the controller only reads, delegates, and selects the view.

risks.risk: The page reads every specialty and every veterinarian on each request, and the product decision excludes paging.
risks.mitigation: Accepted at clinic scale and recorded in ADR 2026-08-16 Consequences; VetRepository.findAll() is already cached under vets.

risks.risk: Reusing existing message keys whose wording carries a different meaning — none currently means "this vet holds no specialty" and would read wrong under a specialty heading.
risks.mitigation: Reuse a key only where the wording means the same thing; otherwise add a new key to messages.properties and to all nine non-English bundles.

risks.risk: Touching the Vet mapping (an inverse mappedBy collection) to reach the holders would change the eager fetch graph and the cached vet list, which the slice's non-goals exclude.
risks.mitigation: ADR 2026-08-16 rules the inverse mapping out; the veterinarian directory and its cache stay untouched.

risks.risk: A hard-coded string in the new template fails I18nPropertiesSyncTest, and a key missing from one bundle fails it too.
risks.mitigation: Every user-facing string goes through #{...}; run ./gradlew test before handing off.

notes: Security and reliability: the route takes no request parameter and no path variable, so no user input crosses into a query — no new trust boundary. Output escaping is Thymeleaf's default, already covered by the XSS row of the threat model. The read is read-only; no repository write method is added, so NG-2 holds structurally. An empty specialties table renders an empty page rather than an error (fail-closed on the empty case). No Security Context or Threat Model row changes, and none was invented. Ordering: specialties by name, veterinarians within a specialty by last name then first name. The PRD records the sort key as open; name order is the narrowest reading and matches the two existing precedents (PetTypeRepository, Vet.getSpecialties). Open question carried forward, not blocking: whether the directory should later gain a visible entry point and a link per veterinarian — the entry carries names only today, so a link needs identity added (ADR 2026-08-16 Consequences). Caching: the new repository is deliberately uncached; a second cache region would extend the unresolved eviction question in system-design.md Open Question 5. Naming comes from ubiquitous-language.md: "Specialty directory" is the confirmed term, so the template is specialtyDirectory.html, not specialtyList.html (the avoid list rejects "Specialty list"). Durable memory written this dispatch: docs/adr/2026-08-16-specialty-directory-read-model.md (new), docs/adr/README.md index row, docs/system-design.md package-structure line, four Contracts rows, the derived-read-model invariant note, and a clause on Open Question 5. No design-doc-autofix records existed to audit.

author: security-reviewer
recommendations: Supply chain: no OWASP Dependency-Check plugin is configured in build.gradle and this reviewer has no network access, so no NVD match ran — that check is not run, not clean. The change set touches no dependency declaration (build.gradle, settings.gradle, and gradle/ are unmodified), so it adds no supply-chain surface; closing the NVD gap is a repository-level task for CI or a human, not a defect of this slice.

Defensive, non-blocking: SpecialtyDirectory.fullName concatenates getFirstName() and getLastName() without a null guard, so a row with a null name would render the literal "null". Bean validation on Vet makes this unreachable through the application's own write paths, and the values are HTML-escaped either way, so this is cosmetic rather than a security defect.
approved_aspects: No injection into data access: SpecialtyRepository.findSpecialties() is a static JPQL string with no parameters and no request-derived value; the read is @Transactional(readOnly = true) and the interface extends the plain Repository marker, so no write path is exposed (least privilege).

No XSS surface introduced: specialtyDirectory.html renders every dynamic value through th:text (entry.specialtyName, veterinarianName, and the #{...} message keys). No th:utext, no inline script, no external resource load, no Thymeleaf preprocessing (__${...}__), no href. Default escaping stays on.

Endpoint exposure is not widened beyond baseline: GET /specialties.html takes no request parameter, no path variable, and no request body. The data it renders (specialty names, veterinarian full names) is already served by /vets.html and /vets, so no new information class reaches an unauthenticated caller.

Mass assignment not applicable and pattern-consistent: the handler binds only Model, so there is no request-bound type to disallow an identifier on. The absence of @InitBinder matches the neighbouring read-only VetController; the binding controllers (Owner, Pet, Visit) keep their disallow lists untouched.
No path traversal: the view name is the private static final constant VIEW_SPECIALTY_DIRECTORY, never composed from caller input.

Thread safety under singleton scope: SpecialtyController holds only final repository references; SpecialtyDirectory and its Entry are records whose compact constructors run List.copyOf, and the shared Comparator is static final and stateless. Nothing mutates the @Cacheable("vets") instances returned by VetRepository.findAll() — SpecialtyDirectory.of only reads them into fresh collections.

No secrets, credentials, or sensitive data added: a diff-wide search for password/secret/token/key/credential material returns nothing in the change set; the eleven message bundles add only display strings.
No unsafe deserialization, shell execution, file I/O, system-tmp use, logging, System.out/System.err, or regex added anywhere in the change set.

Resource footprint unchanged in kind: both reads are unpaged full-table reads, but VetRepository.findAll() is the pre-existing cached read already used by /vets, and Specialty is a small reference table with an EAGER association, so no new unbounded-allocation path is introduced.
